campgrounds.name: Rob Hill Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Opens in February for entire season (Apr-Oct) at 9:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Group / Tent camping (up to 30 people per site)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed for winter (open Apr–Oct only). Wet cypress coastal fog, crisp ocean breeze.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Presidio Promenade, Battery Godfrey, Immigrant Point, Coastal Trail to Baker Beach
campgrounds.description: The only public campground in San Francisco! Perched in a cypress grove overlooking Baker Beach and the Pacific Ocean.

campgrounds.name: Angel Island East Bay & Kayak Camps
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in & Kayak landing campsites (Sites 7-9 & Kayak Group Site)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; direct paddle craft landing access at Kayak Camp for self-contained sea kayakers.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Perimeter Trail, Quarry Beach, Angel Island Ferry dock at Ayala Cove
campgrounds.description: Sheltered bayside camping with boat/kayak landing beach and views of the East Bay.

campgrounds.name: Angel Island Ridge Campsites
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in ridge primitive sites (Sites 1, 2, 3)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; brisk bay winds, jaw-dropping panoramic views of the Golden Gate Bridge and SF nighttime skyline.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mt. Caroline Livermore peak, Perimeter Trail, Immigration Station
campgrounds.description: Unbeatable nighttime panorama of San Francisco skyscrapers lit up across the water.

campgrounds.name: Kirby Cove Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov (extremely competitive)
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites (1 day-use group site)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; chilly coastal winds, heavy fog, but stunning crisp winter sunsets framing Golden Gate Bridge.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Golden Gate Bridge bluff views, Hawk Hill, Coastal Trail, Black Sands Beach
campgrounds.description: Unrivaled view directly facing the Golden Gate Bridge and SF skyline from a sheltered beach cove. Sells out within milliseconds of release.

campgrounds.name: Angel Island Sunrise Campsites
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in east-facing primitive sites (Sites 4, 5, 6)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sheltered from western winds; spectacular morning sunrise over the East Bay hills.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Perimeter Trail, East Garrison historic military barracks, Fort McDowell
campgrounds.description: East-facing campsites looking across the bay toward Berkeley, Oakland, and Mount Diablo.

campgrounds.name: Bicentennial Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites (100-200m from car)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; cold ocean winds, vault toilets only, pack all water in.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rodeo Lagoon, Point Bonita Lighthouse, Battery Mendell, Coastal Trail
campgrounds.description: Marin Headlands ocean vistas, easiest walk-in camp in the Headlands near historic batteries and Rodeo Beach.

campgrounds.name: Hawkcamp Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Backcountry hike-in tent sites (3 mi uphill hike via Bobcat or Miwok trail)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; exposed high-ridge backcountry site with strong marine winds; bring all water and wind-rated tent.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Bobcat Trail, Miwok Trail, Coastal Trail, Hawk Hill raptor migration
campgrounds.description: Perched high on a ridge at 1,000 ft elevation with panoramic views of the Marin Headlands, SF Bay, and the Pacific.

campgrounds.name: Haypress Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Hike-in backcountry tent sites (0.75 mi hike from Tennessee Valley parking)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; pack in all water; muddy trails after winter rains. Very peaceful valley setting.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Tennessee Valley Trail, Tennessee Beach, Coastal Trail, Rhubarb Trail
campgrounds.description: Tucked into the lush floor of Tennessee Valley. An easy 0.75-mile hike from the trailhead makes it ideal for beginner backpackers.

campgrounds.name: Bootjack Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 100% First-Come, First-Served year-round. Arrive early Friday morning for weekend stays.
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites in sheltered redwood and bay laurel canyon
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open 365 days a year; quiet, secluded redwood canyon with flowing creek in winter and spring.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Bootjack Trail, Mountain Theater, Old Mine Trail, Dipsea Trail connection
campgrounds.description: Located 0.7 miles east of Pantoll along Panoramic Highway. Quieter and more sheltered than Pantoll, with direct access to Bootjack Trail.

campgrounds.name: Pantoll Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 100% First-Come, First-Served year-round (open 365 days). For weekend stays arrive by Friday 8:00 AM.
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites under towering Douglas firs and coastal oaks
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open 365 days a year! Winter brings rushing waterfalls on Steep Ravine and Cataract trails, lush green moss, and fewer crowds.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Dipsea Trail, Steep Ravine Trail, Matt Davis Trail, Stinson Beach, Cataract Falls
campgrounds.description: The premier trail hub of Mt. Tamalpais. Direct trailhead access to the famed Dipsea Trail, Steep Ravine Trail, and Matt Davis Trail.

campgrounds.name: Steep Ravine Environmental Campsites
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive walk-in bluff tent sites (100-300 yards from parking)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; dramatic winter surf, open marine exposure. Bring heavy-duty tent stakes.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rocky Point, Dipsea Trail, Stinson Beach, Steep Ravine Trail
campgrounds.description: Camp on the coastal terrace bluffs overlooking crashing Pacific breakers and rocky tidepools.

campgrounds.name: Steep Ravine Cabins
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia (sells out in under 2 seconds)
campgrounds.site_types: Historic rustic wood oceanfront cabins with wood-burning stoves
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; wood-burning cast-iron stoves keep historic rustic cabins cozy during dramatic Pacific winter rainstorms.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rocky Point tidepools, Dipsea Trail, Stinson Beach, Steep Ravine redwoods
campgrounds.description: Perched directly on rugged Pacific cliffs on Rocky Point. No electricity; kerosene or wood stove heating. California's most coveted stay.

campgrounds.name: China Camp State Park (Back Ranch Meadows)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling on ReserveCalifornia / Friends of China Camp
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites (100-300 yards from parking in oak meadow)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sheltered from coastal fog, mild winter temperatures along San Pablo Bay.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Shoreline Trail, historic 1880s Chinese shrimp fishing village, San Pablo Bay kayak launch
campgrounds.description: Tucked into warm, sun-drenched oak and bay laurel woodlands along San Pablo Bay. 15 miles of mountain bike singletrack.

campgrounds.name: Anthony Chabot Regional Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 12 weeks (84 days) rolling in advance on EBRPD portal
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV hookup sites, hike-in backpack sites
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; eucalyptus and pine forest above Lake Chabot; easy quick getaway.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lake Chabot loop trail, Honker Bay, Skyline National Recreation Trail, Redwood Regional Park
campgrounds.description: Forested ridges above Lake Chabot with miles of hiking, mountain biking, and dog-friendly trails.

campgrounds.name: Half Moon Bay State Beach (Francis Beach)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Tent, RV hookup & electric sites, hike-and-bike
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; huge winter swells at nearby Mavericks, brisk coastal walks on paved bluffs, heated coin showers.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Coastside Trail (paved bluff path), Mavericks surf break, Pillar Point Harbor, Purisima Creek
campgrounds.description: Right on the coastal bluffs above Francis Beach with crashing waves, beachcombing, and paved biking on the Coastside Trail.

campgrounds.name: Samuel P. Taylor State Park (Creekside & Madrone)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Standard drive-in tent, RV (no hookups), plus Madrone rustic cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter coho salmon spawning runs in Lagunitas Creek, roaring creek, cool redwood canyon floor.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Cross Marin Bike Trail, Barnabe Mountain, Pioneer Redwood Tree Trail, Lagunitas Creek salmon run
campgrounds.description: Lush old-growth redwood grove along Lagunitas Creek. Paved car-free path connects directly to West Marin.

campgrounds.name: Point Reyes: Wildcat Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Hike-in backcountry campsites (5.5 - 6.3 mi hike from Palomarin or Bear Valley)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter brings thundering surf, whale migration watching, and lush green coastal bluffs.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Alamere Falls, Wildcat Beach, Ocean Lake Loop, Bass Lake swimming hole
campgrounds.description: Located in an open meadow plateau steps from the beach and only 1 mile south of tidefall waterfall Alamere Falls.

campgrounds.name: Point Reyes: Glen Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Hike-in backcountry campsites (4.6 mi hike from Bear Valley Visitor Center)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; deep quiet forest sheltered from coastal ocean fog and high winds.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Glen Trail, Stewart Trail, Bear Valley Trail, Mt. Wittenberg summit
campgrounds.description: Tucked into a quiet valley among towering Douglas firs and bishop pines. No ocean view, but maximum wind protection and solitude.

campgrounds.name: Mount Diablo: Live Oak Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent sites nestled in oaks near sandstone outcrops
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sheltered from high summit winds, pleasant spring oak canopy.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rock City sandstone mazes, Sentinel Rock, Trail Through Time
campgrounds.description: Nestled below Rock City among mossy sandstone boulders and ancient valley oaks. Great for scrambling and exploring caves.

campgrounds.name: Mount Diablo: Juniper Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & small RV sites at 3,000 ft elevation
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; high elevation brings crisp winter sunsets over SF Bay and sunrise over the Sierra crest.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mount Diablo Summit (3,849 ft, 40-county view), Summit Trail, Grand Loop Trail
campgrounds.description: Perched at 3,000 feet on the shoulder of Mount Diablo. Breathtaking sunset views across the entire San Francisco Bay Area.

campgrounds.name: Point Reyes: Sky Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Hike-in backcountry campsites (1.4 mi uphill hike from Sky Trailhead)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sweeping ocean sunsets overlooking Drakes Bay and Point Reyes headlands.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mount Wittenberg Trail, Sky Trail, Meadow Trail, Woodward Valley Trail
campgrounds.description: Perched on the western slope of Mount Wittenberg at 1,025 ft. Spectacular views of Drakes Bay, the Pacific, and coastal fog layers.

campgrounds.name: Point Reyes: Coast Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Hike-in & Bike-in backcountry campsites (1.8 mi easy walk/bike from Laguna)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; broad sandy beach, coastal tidepools, easy bike-in camping option.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Santa Maria Beach, Coast Trail to Sculptured Beach, Laguna Trail, Fire Lane Trail
campgrounds.description: Nestled in a grassy coastal hollow 200 meters from Santa Maria Beach. The easiest backcountry camp to reach in Point Reyes.

campgrounds.name: Point Reyes: Tomales Bay Boat-In Camps
campgrounds.reservation_window: 3 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Boat-in only wilderness beach campsites along west shore of Tomales Bay
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; kayak-in only; must carry all fresh water and pack out all human waste (portable toilet required).
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Tomales Bay paddling, bioluminescent night kayaking, tule elk viewing on Tomales Point
campgrounds.description: Wilderness beach camping accessible only by kayak, canoe, or boat. Camp on pristine sandy beaches like Marshall Beach and Tomales Beach.

campgrounds.name: Memorial Park Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 180 days (6 months) in advance on San Mateo County Parks reservation system
campgrounds.site_types: Tent and RV sites along Pescadero Creek under tall redwoods
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; high winter creek levels, cool damp redwood forest, very quiet and atmospheric.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Pescadero Creek swimming holes, Mount Ellen Trail, Pomponio Creek, Pescadero Marsh
campgrounds.description: Beloved century-old park surrounded by towering coast redwoods and swimming holes in Pescadero Creek.

campgrounds.name: Portola Redwoods State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Standard drive-in, walk-in, and backpack camp
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; deep quiet canyon with winter creek cascades and lush moss.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Peters Creek Old Growth Grove, Tip Toe Falls, Slate Creek Trail, Iverson Trail
campgrounds.description: Deep, quiet, rugged redwood canyon with giant trees, ferns, and one of the finest ancient groves in the Bay Area.

campgrounds.name: Butano State Park (Ben Ries Campground)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent sites, walk-in sites, backpack trail camp
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; secluded redwood canyon cloaked in coastal fog and moss, tucked away near Pescadero.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Ano Nuevo State Park (elephant seals), Candelabra Tree, Goat Hill Trail, Jackson Flats
campgrounds.description: A quiet, lush redwood canyon sanctuary. Excellent trails through deep fern groves and sandstone ridgetops.

campgrounds.name: Del Valle Regional Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 12 weeks (84 days) rolling on EBRPD portal
campgrounds.site_types: Tent, RV with water/sewer/electric, group sites
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; pleasant sunny winter/spring camping; warm swimming in summer.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: 5-mile reservoir kayak/paddle, Ohlone Wilderness Trail trailhead, Rose Peak (3,817 ft)
campgrounds.description: Surrounded by oak-covered hills with a 5-mile long reservoir for swimming, boating, and deep wilderness backpacking.

campgrounds.name: Sanborn County Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling on Santa Clara County Parks portal
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent campsites tucked under coastal redwoods
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; mild redwood climate, fast access from South Bay.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Skyline Trail, Castle Rock State Park sandstone climbing spires, Sanborn Creek trail, Indian Rock
campgrounds.description: Lush redwood forest tucked onto the eastern slope of the Santa Cruz Mountains above Saratoga. Direct trail link to Castle Rock.

campgrounds.name: Big Basin: Sempervirens Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 60-day rolling window on ReserveCalifornia (limited reopening post-CZU fire)
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in & walk-in tent sites along Sempervirens Creek
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round (rebuilding); winter rain feeds Berry Creek and Sempervirens waterfalls, vivid green redwood rebirth.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Redwood Loop, Berry Creek Falls trail reconstruction, Skyline-to-the-Sea trail, Waddell Creek
campgrounds.description: California's oldest state park (1902). Resilient ancient redwoods rebounding with vibrant green sprouts.

campgrounds.name: Big Basin: Blooms Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 60-day rolling window on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in campsites shaded by surviving ancient redwood sentinels
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round with seasonal reopening schedule; peaceful redwood creekside setting.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Blooms Creek Trail, Pine Mountain, Opal Creek, Gazos Creek
campgrounds.description: Located in the upper Blooms Creek basin surrounded by resilient coast redwoods.

campgrounds.name: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
campgrounds.agency: California State Parks / Sonoma Ecology Ctr
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, small RV, plus luxury glamping tents
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; dark skies for astronomy; winter creek waterfalls flow vigorously.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Bald Mountain summit (view Sierra & SF on clear days), Sonoma Creek Falls, Ferguson Observatory
campgrounds.description: Sonoma Valley gem with dark skies, public observatory stargazing, waterfalls, and steep panoramic climbs.

campgrounds.name: Brannan Island State Recreation Area
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites, boat launch, group sites
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; mild delta winter weather, world-class striped bass & sturgeon fishing.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta sloughs, windy kayak trails, striped bass & sturgeon fishing, windsurfing on Sherman Island
campgrounds.description: Island paradise in the maze of the Delta. Ideal basecamp for kayak exploring, sailing, and warm delta river breezes.

campgrounds.name: Lake Berryessa (Pleasure Cove Marina)
campgrounds.reservation_window: Rolling advance reservations on Pleasure Cove portal
campgrounds.site_types: Lakeside tent, full-hookup RV sites, and rustic cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; pleasant mild winter weather, quiet lake views.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Monticello Dam Glory Hole spillway, Smittle Creek Trail, swimming coves, boat wakeboarding
campgrounds.description: Expansive warm-water reservoir nestled in eastern Napa County hills with full-service marina and lakefront tenting.

campgrounds.name: Bothe-Napa Valley State Park
campgrounds.agency: California State Parks / Napa County Reg Parks
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV, historic cabins & yurts
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; historic restored cabins provide cozy winter stays in wine country.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Ritchey Creek Trail, Coyote Peak, Bale Grist Mill State Historic Park, Napa Valley Vine Trail
campgrounds.description: Camp nestled among redwoods and maple in the heart of Napa wine country; spring-fed swimming pool in summer.

campgrounds.name: Sonoma Coast: Bodega Dunes Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites sheltered behind tall coastal dunes with hot showers
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sand dunes provide shelter from high winter coastal winds; coin-operated hot showers.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Bodega Head whale watching, Salmon Creek surf break, Bodega Dunes trail
campgrounds.description: Spacious campsites tucked behind coastal dunes with boardwalk paths leading directly out to expansive sandy beaches.

campgrounds.name: Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV (no hookups) in pine and oak ridge
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; river levels rise in winter; majestic old-growth loop trail.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Old Growth Redwood Grove, Garden of Eden swimming hole, Roaring Camp steam train, Fall Creek unit
campgrounds.description: Ancient 275-foot redwoods, sandy pine ridges, and freshwater river swimming in the San Lorenzo River.

campgrounds.name: Sonoma Coast: Wright's Beach Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia (sells out in seconds)
campgrounds.site_types: Beachfront drive-in campsites steps from crashing Pacific surf
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; watch thundering Pacific winter breakers crash right in front of your campfire.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Kortum Trail (bluff hike to Blind Beach), Duncan's Landing, Goat Rock seal colony
campgrounds.description: Step directly from your campsite onto the sand. The most coveted oceanfront drive-in campsites in Northern California.

campgrounds.name: Sonoma Coast: Pomo Canyon Environmental Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in campsites in peaceful second-growth redwood canyon
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sheltered inland redwood canyon, escape coastal wind while staying 2 miles from ocean.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Pomo Canyon Trail to Shell Beach, Red Hill Trail, Russian River mouth
campgrounds.description: A hidden redwood sanctuary tucked into the hills just behind the coastal bluffs. Direct access to the Pomo Canyon Trail.

campgrounds.name: Uvas Canyon County Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months in advance on Santa Clara County Parks portal
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent campsites nestled along Swanson Creek
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter and spring are the premier seasons as winter rains turn all six canyon waterfalls into roaring cascades.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Waterfall Loop Trail (Black Rock Falls, Basin Falls, Upper Falls), Swanson Creek, Alec Canyon Trail
campgrounds.description: Lush canyon wonderland packed with six multi-tiered natural waterfalls cascading through mossy ferns and Douglas firs.

campgrounds.name: Austin Creek SRA (Bullfrog Pond)
campgrounds.agency: California State Parks / Stewards of Coast & Redwoods
campgrounds.reservation_window: Rolling on Hipcamp / Stewards of Coast & Redwoods portal
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in primitive tent & backpack trail camps
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; high elevation ridge camp above Guerneville fog layer.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve, Gilliam Creek, East Ridge Trail, Russian River paddling
campgrounds.description: Perched high above Guerneville and Armstrong Redwoods; rugged oak savanna, rolling ridges, and serene starry skies.

campgrounds.name: New Brighton State Beach
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Beach bluff tent & RV sites (premium oceanfront hookups)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; coastal bluff camping overlooking the entire crescent of Monterey Bay.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Capitola Village, Forest of Nisene Marks State Park, Monterey Bay coastal bluff trails
campgrounds.description: Forested bluff campsites looking out across Monterey Bay; dolphins and otters often visible directly from camp.

campgrounds.name: Henry W. Coe: Coe Ranch Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in sites at 2,600 ft ridge near headquarters
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; crisp winter camping with emerald green hills and starry night skies.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Pine Ridge Trail, Middle Ridge, Monument Peak, Hunting Hollow
campgrounds.description: Perched at 2,600 feet at the park headquarters entrance of Northern California's largest state park (87,000 acres).

campgrounds.name: Henry W. Coe: Wilderness Backpacking
campgrounds.reservation_window: Self-issued backpacking registration at park headquarters kiosk upon arrival
campgrounds.site_types: Dispersed and designated wilderness trail camps (Mississippi Lake, Poverty Flat)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter and spring are prime backpacking seasons when seasonal streams and lakes are full.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mississippi Lake, Poverty Flat, Orestimba Wilderness, Mount Sizer (The Shortcut)
campgrounds.description: Over 87,000 acres of open Diablo Range wilderness backpacking solitude with remote fishing lakes and wildflower ridges.

campgrounds.name: Mount Madonna County Park (Campground & Yurts)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months in advance on Santa Clara County Parks portal
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV sites, and 5 rustic canvas yurts
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; canvas yurts provide heated winter glamping under the redwoods.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Henry Miller historic estate ruins, giant redwood groves, white fallow deer sanctuary, Mt. Madonna archery range
campgrounds.description: Majestic coast redwood forest perched atop the Santa Cruz mountain ridge between Gilroy and Watsonville.

campgrounds.name: Lake Sonoma Recreation Area
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in campsites at Warm Springs + 15 primitive Boat-In/Hike-In wilderness camps
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; boat-in camping along 50 miles of winding shoreline.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lake Sonoma Marina, Little Flat trail, Warm Springs Dam, Dry Creek Valley wineries
campgrounds.description: Warm water lake tucked into Sonoma hills; unique boat-in boat camping along 50 miles of winding shoreline.

campgrounds.name: Salt Point: Gerstle Cove Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in ocean bluff sites just above Gerstle Cove marine reserve
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; ocean bluff perch with crashing winter waves, tide pools, and crisp sunset views.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Tafoni sandstone formations, Gerstle Cove Marine Reserve, Salt Point bluff trail
campgrounds.description: Perched on open coastal bluffs above Gerstle Cove Marine Reserve. World-class abalone and scuba diving location.

campgrounds.name: Salt Point: Woodside Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in forest sites tucked among bishop pines and huckleberry
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; densely forested setting provides wind shelter during coastal storms.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Pygmy Forest Trail, Central Trail to ocean bluffs, Fisk Mill Cove
campgrounds.description: Located on the east side of Highway 1 nestled in a dense bishop pine and rhododendron forest with trail to Pygmy Forest.

campgrounds.name: Fremont Peak: Valley View Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive ridge campsites with expansive valley and ocean sunset views
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; unobstructed sunset views across the Salinas Valley out to Monterey Bay.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Summit Trail, Valley View Trail, dark sky stargazing
campgrounds.description: High ridge camping with sweeping 360-degree vistas across Monterey Bay and Salinas Valley. World-renowned dark sky astronomy.

campgrounds.name: Fremont Peak: Oak Point Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive drive-in & tent sites tucked under valley oaks
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; high ridge winds and occasional light snow dustings at 3,169 ft. Crystal-clear winter skies for astronomy.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Fremont Peak Trail to 3,169-ft summit, Fremont Peak Astronomical Observatory, San Juan Bautista historic mission
campgrounds.description: Sheltered camping under coastal oaks just below the summit of Fremont Peak. Direct trail to astronomical observatory.

campgrounds.name: Clear Lake: Kelsey Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites along creek channel with boat launch
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; world-class bass fishing during winter and spring months.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mount Konocti dormant volcano summit hike (Wright Peak 4,299 ft), Kelsey Creek nature trail, bass fishing
campgrounds.description: Situated on the quiet shores of California's oldest natural freshwater lake under the volcanic shadow of Mount Konocti.

campgrounds.name: Clear Lake: Cole Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites in shaded oak woodland near swim beach
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; shaded camping near swimming beach and boat marina.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Cole Creek trail, swim beach, kayak rentals, Mount Konocti views
campgrounds.description: Wooded campsites under oak canopy with easy walking access to the sandy swimming beach.

campgrounds.name: San Luis Reservoir: Basalt Campground
campgrounds.park_name: San Luis Reservoir State Rec Area
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites in sheltered basalt canyon
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; mild winter and spring camping with rolling green hills and spring wildflowers.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Basalt Hill Trail, Pacheco Pass historic stagecoach trail, spring wildflower hillsides, reservoir boating
campgrounds.description: Sheltered basalt canyon below massive San Luis Dam near Pacheco Pass; gateway to warm central valley water sports and rolling hills.

campgrounds.name: San Luis Reservoir: San Luis Creek Camp
campgrounds.park_name: San Luis Reservoir State Rec Area
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Waterfront campsites on O'Neill Forebay with boat launch
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; lakefront recreation on O'Neill Forebay.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: O'Neill Forebay water sports, striped bass fishing, shoreline trail
campgrounds.description: Direct water access on the O'Neill Forebay with windsurfing, boat launching, and swimming beach.

campgrounds.name: Hendy Woods State Park (Campground & Cabins)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites, plus 4 rustic Azalea cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; rustic cabins offer heating for cozy winter redwood stays.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Big Hendy Old Growth Redwood Grove (1,000-year-old trees), Navarro River swimming, Anderson Valley Pinot Noir
campgrounds.description: Less crowded old-growth redwood sanctuary in Anderson Valley along the gentle Navarro River.

campgrounds.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia (very high demand)
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV (no hookups), walk-in riverside sites
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter rains awaken Pfeiffer Falls, rushing Big Sur River, cozy campfire evenings.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Buzzard's Roost Trail, Big Sur River Gorge, Pfeiffer Falls, Valley View Trail, Pfeiffer Beach purple sands
campgrounds.description: The quintessential Big Sur experience along the redwood-canopied Big Sur River with natural river swimming holes.

campgrounds.name: Pinnacles National Park Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Tent, RV with electrical hookups, tent cabins, group sites
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter is prime season! Mild hiking weather in the 60s, lush moss in Bear Gulch Caves, active condor flights.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: High Peaks Trail (carved rock steps into volcanic spires), Bear Gulch Cave (talus cave), Condor viewing
campgrounds.description: Only campground in California's newest National Park; home to soaring California Condors, talus caves, and swimming pool.

campgrounds.name: Calaveras Big Trees State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites, cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter brings magical snowshoeing through the North Grove among massive snow-covered Giant Sequoias.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: North Grove Giant Sequoias, South Grove Trail, Stanislaus River swimming at Beaver Creek
campgrounds.description: Home to ancient Giant Sequoias (Sequoiadendron giganteum) up to 3,000 years old along the crystal Stanislaus River.

campgrounds.name: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia (only 2 walk-in sites!)
campgrounds.site_types: Environmental walk-in cliffside tent sites (Sites 1 & 2)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; only two walk-in sites perched on the cliffs overlooking McWay Falls and turquoise Pacific cove. Sells out instantly.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: McWay Falls (80-ft waterfall into turquoise Pacific cove), Ewoldsen Trail, Partington Cove
campgrounds.description: Legendary cliff-edge campsites perched directly over the Pacific near McWay Falls. Pure coastal magic.

campgrounds.name: Van Damme State Park Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in and walk-in campsites in Little River redwood canyon
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; sheltered canyon camping near sea caves and Pygmy forest.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Fern Canyon Trail, Pygmy Forest boardwalk, sea kayaking in Van Damme cove
campgrounds.description: Campsites along Little River in a sheltered canyon; kayak tours into sea caves launch directly from the park's beach.

campgrounds.name: Russian Gulch State Park Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Standard drive-in campsites in lush fern-draped canyon
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter rains transform Russian Gulch Falls into a roaring cascade; dramatic sea waves at Devil's Punchbowl.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Devil's Punchbowl sea chasm, Russian Gulch 36-ft Waterfall Trail, Frederick W. Panhorst Bridge, coastal headlands
campgrounds.description: Mendocino coastal paradise: towering sea-bridge, dramatic blowholes, lush fern canyons, and ocean headlands.

campgrounds.name: Kirk Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov + several First-Come First-Served sites
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in bluff tent & RV sites directly overlooking Pacific Ocean
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; dramatic open bluff ocean views, whale watching with binoculars from your tent.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Vicente Flat Trail (into Ventana Wilderness), Sand Dollar Beach, Mill Creek cove
campgrounds.description: Every campsite has an unobstructed, panoramic view of the Pacific Ocean from an open coastal bluff.

campgrounds.name: Prewitt Ridge Dispersed Area
campgrounds.reservation_window: No reservations - 100% Free Dispersed Camping (High clearance AWD/4WD recommended, bring all water)
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive dispersed rim campsites at 3,200 ft elevation
campgrounds.winter_profile: Primitive dirt road (Nacimiento-Fergusson / Coast Ridge Rd). 4WD required, highly impassable when muddy in winter. Zero water.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Prewitt Loop Trail, Ventana Wilderness, 3,200-ft cliff drop overlooking marine fog bank
campgrounds.description: High-altitude coastal ridge camping 3,200 feet directly above the Pacific Ocean. Sleep above the clouds with jaw-dropping sunsets.

campgrounds.name: Plaskett Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites in Monterey pine grove
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; grassy park-like sites sheltered by tall pines, steps from Sand Dollar Beach.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Sand Dollar Beach (largest sandy beach in Big Sur), Jade Cove, Willow Creek
campgrounds.description: Park-like grassy setting under giant Monterey pines just across Highway 1 from Sand Dollar Beach.

campgrounds.name: Mokelumne Wilderness: Caples Lake Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Tent and RV campsites along Caples Lake shoreline under lodgepole pine
campgrounds.winter_profile: Heavy winter snow; Kirkwood Mountain Resort is just 5 miles away on Hwy 88.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Caples Lake trail, Emigrant Lake, Kirkwood Mountain Resort, Carson Pass
campgrounds.description: Situated on the forested northern shore of Caples Lake with trout fishing, kayak launching, and views of Round Top.

campgrounds.name: Desolation Wilderness: Lake Aloha Backcountry
campgrounds.reservation_window: Wilderness backpacking quota permits open 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Glaciated granite wilderness campsites on islands & peninsulas across 63,960 acres
campgrounds.winter_profile: Frozen under thick ice and heavy alpine snowpack Nov–May. Serious mountaineering terrain.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Pyramid Peak (9,983 ft), Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), Susie Lake, Heather Lake, Mosquito Pass
campgrounds.description: California's most famous glaciated alpine lake: a shallow reservoir dotted with hundreds of white granite islands beneath Pyramid Peak.

campgrounds.name: Mokelumne Wilderness: Woods Lake Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: Woods Lake on Recreation.gov (6 months rolling); Wilderness backpacking self-issued at Carson Pass
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent sites at Woods Lake (8,200 ft elevation)
campgrounds.winter_profile: HOME OF CARSON PASS SNO-PARK: Carson Pass (8,574 ft) is one of the highest maintained winter passes in California (Hwy 88). Heavy snowfall makes it a premier haven for snowshoers and XC skiers trekking to frozen Frog Lake.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Round Top peak (10,381 ft), Winnemucca Lake wildflower meadows, Frog Lake, Fourth of July Lake, Pacific Crest Trail
campgrounds.description: Famous for California's most spectacular alpine wildflower displays in July along the trail to Winnemucca Lake and Round Top (10,381 ft).

campgrounds.name: Emerald Bay: Eagle Point Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites on forested bluff overlooking Emerald Bay
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed Nov–Apr due to heavy snow and cliffside road conditions. World-famous viewpoint above Fannette Island.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rubicon Trail, Vikingsholm Castle, Eagle Falls, Emerald Bay Lookout
campgrounds.description: Perched on the forested granite cliffs looking directly down into the azure waters of Emerald Bay and Fannette Island.

campgrounds.name: Emerald Bay: Boat-In Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Lake-access boat-in campsites on northern shore of Emerald Bay
campgrounds.winter_profile: Accessible only by boat or kayak across Emerald Bay or by hiking in from D.L. Bliss.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Emerald Bay paddle routes, Fannette Island tea house ruins, Rubicon Point
campgrounds.description: Spectacular boat-in camping situated right on the quiet northern shoreline of Emerald Bay near the mouth of the bay.

campgrounds.name: Desolation Wilderness: Bayview Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 100% First-Come, First-Served trailhead camping ($20). Wilderness permits on Rec.gov.
campgrounds.site_types: Trailhead tent campsites directly at Bayview / Desolation trailhead
campgrounds.winter_profile: EXTREME ALPINE WINTER WILDERNESS: Buried under 10–25 feet of snow in winter. Staging area for mountaineers climbing Mount Tallac (9,735 ft).
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mount Tallac summit (panoramic view of all Lake Tahoe), Granite Lake, Maggie's Peaks, Desolation Wilderness
campgrounds.description: Trailhead campground perched directly on the granite ridge above Emerald Bay. Gateway into Desolation Wilderness.

campgrounds.name: Emigrant Wilderness: Kennedy Meadows
campgrounds.reservation_window: Campground is 100% FCFS ($20); Wilderness permits are FREE and self-issued at Summit Ranger Station
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in riverside campsites at pack station + 113,000 acres of wilderness backpacking
campgrounds.winter_profile: Sonora Pass (Hwy 108) closes completely with the first major winter storm (Nov to May). Inaccessible by car in deep winter.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Relief Reservoir, Kennedy Lake, Sonora Pass (9,624 ft) PCT crossing, Leavitt Falls, Columns of the Giants
campgrounds.description: The uncrowded sister to Yosemite. Smooth glaciated granite bowls, clear trout streams (Middle Fork Stanislaus River), and sprawling trails.

campgrounds.name: D.L. Bliss State Park Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in campsites tucked among giant granite boulders near lake
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed in winter under 6 to 10 feet of snow.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rubicon Trail, Calawee Cove beach, Balancing Rock trail, Lester Beach
campgrounds.description: Home to Calawee Cove beach—one of Lake Tahoe's most beautiful hidden boulder coves. Starting point of the cliffside Rubicon Trail.

campgrounds.name: Meeks Bay Campground & Resort
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov (extremely coveted)
campgrounds.site_types: Tent and RV campsites steps from shoreline
campgrounds.winter_profile: Vehicle campground closed Nov–Apr under feet of snow. Serves as winter backcountry departure point for snowshoers entering the snowbound Meeks Creek valley into Desolation Wilderness.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Meeks Creek Trail (into northern Desolation Wilderness & Rubicon Lake), Rubicon Trail, Sugar Pine Point
campgrounds.description: Widely acclaimed as the prettiest beach setting on Lake Tahoe. Golden sand, crystal azure water, and direct trailhead into the granite heart of Desolation Wilderness.

campgrounds.name: Sugar Pine Point: General Creek Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites (Plowed loops in winter with heated modern restrooms!)
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Aug (Summer) & Jan – Feb (Winter snow camping)
campgrounds.winter_profile: THE WINTER CROWN JEWEL: One of the only campgrounds in Lake Tahoe open all winter for official plowed snow camping! Heated modern restrooms with flush toilets and hot running water. Directly adjacent to 12+ miles of marked/groomed Nordic ski and snowshoe trails along General Creek (1960 Winter Olympic Nordic site).
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: General Creek Trail, D.L. Bliss / Rubicon Trail connection, Ehrman Mansion, Olympic 1960 Nordic trails, Sugar Pine beach
campgrounds.description: Lake Tahoe's premier year-round state park. In winter, camp in deep powder snow with heated restrooms; in summer, enjoy quiet sandy beaches beneath towering 200-foot sugar pines.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: Wawona Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Released on 15th of each month on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Campsites along South Fork Merced River near Mariposa Grove
campgrounds.winter_profile: Loop A stays open year-round in winter; snowshoeing among the Giant Sequoias in Mariposa Grove is extraordinary.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias (Grizzly Giant, California Tunnel Tree), Chilnualna Falls, swinging bridge
campgrounds.description: Located along the South Fork of the Merced River near the historic Wawona Hotel and the Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias.

campgrounds.name: Blackwood Canyon Sno-Park Staging Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: CA Sno-Park Permit ($15 day / $40 season) Nov 1 to May 30
campgrounds.site_types: Plowed winter staging area for backcountry ski touring, snowmobiling & snowshoeing
campgrounds.winter_profile: NORTH TAHOE WINTER EPICENTER: Plowed parking staging area for snowmobiling up Blackwood Canyon to Barker Pass (PCT), backcountry ski touring to Ellis Peak (8,740 ft), and snowshoeing along Blackwood Creek. Requires California Sno-Park permit.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Barker Pass, Ellis Peak (8,740 ft), Pacific Crest Trail winter route, Blackwood Creek
campgrounds.description: Winter backcountry departure hub for North Lake Tahoe's most expansive alpine terrain.

campgrounds.name: Kaspian Campground (Tent-Only / West Shore)
campgrounds.agency: US Forest Service (Lake Tahoe Basin MU)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Intimate tent-only campsites nestled in Jeffrey pines across from lake
campgrounds.winter_profile: Campground closed in winter, but directly adjacent to Blackwood Canyon Sno-Park for winter backcountry staging.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Blackwood Canyon, Barker Pass (PCT), Ellis Peak, Eagle Rock volcanic vista hike
campgrounds.description: Intimate 9-site tent-only campground directly across Highway 89 from Lake Tahoe with direct paved bicycle trail.

campgrounds.name: Sonora Pass: Baker & Deadman Camps
campgrounds.reservation_window: 100% First-Come, First-Served along Highway 108 corridor
campgrounds.site_types: Riverside campsites shaded by Jeffrey pine along Middle Fork Stanislaus River
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed Nov–May due to seasonal closure of Sonora Pass (Hwy 108).
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Sonora Pass granite peaks, Saint Mary's Pass trail, Pacific Crest Trail
campgrounds.description: Beautiful high-altitude forested campsites along rushing mountain rivers directly on the Sonora Pass scenic highway route.

campgrounds.name: William Kent Campground (North Lake Tahoe)
campgrounds.agency: US Forest Service (Lake Tahoe Basin MU)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent, RV sites (some electric hookups), yurt sites
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Aug (Peak North Lake Tahoe beach season)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed for vehicle camping in winter. Serves as a prime access point: 10 minutes to Palisades Tahoe, 5 minutes to Tahoe City Winter Sports Park (groomed XC skiing, ice skating).
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Tahoe Rim Trail (Ward Creek trailhead), Stanford Rock trail, Page Meadows mountain biking, Tahoe City marina
campgrounds.description: The best-located federal campground on North Lake Tahoe. Minutes from Tahoe City's cafes and lakeside pathways, with beach access across the street.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: Camp 4 (Climbers Camp)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 1-day advance daily lottery on Recreation.gov ($10/person/night)
campgrounds.site_types: Shared walk-in tent campsites beneath granite boulders
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter walk-up registration at kiosk; quiet and peaceful under snow.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Columbia Rock, Upper Yosemite Falls trail, El Capitan Meadow, Midnight Lightning boulder
campgrounds.description: National Register of Historic Places site. The spiritual home of world rock climbing beneath El Capitan and Yosemite Falls.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: Lower Pines Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Released on 15th of each month at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites along the tranquil Merced River
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed Nov–Mar. Opens in spring as snowmelt fills the Merced River.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Merced River beaches, Curry Village, Mist Trail, Yosemite Valley Shuttle
campgrounds.description: Intimate campground in Yosemite Valley with beautiful river-facing campsites directly beneath Half Dome.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: Upper Pines Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Released on 15th of each month at 7:00 AM PT for 5 months ahead on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites in Yosemite Valley along Merced River
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round! Winter in Yosemite Valley brings snow-dusted granite walls, ice skating in Half Dome village, and frozen waterfalls. Tire chains often required on Valley roads.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mist Trail (Vernal & Nevada Falls), Half Dome cables, Mirror Lake, John Muir Trail, Glacier Point
campgrounds.description: The flagship campground in Yosemite Valley. Located at the foot of Half Dome and Glacier Point, steps from the Mist Trail and Happy Isles.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: North Pines Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Released on 15th of each month at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in sites at confluence of Merced River and Tenaya Creek
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed Nov–Mar due to winter river flooding and snow.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Tenaya Creek, Mirror Lake trail, Washington Column, Half Dome views
campgrounds.description: Nestled beneath the sheer rock wall of Washington Column and Royal Arches where Tenaya Creek flows into the Merced River.

campgrounds.name: Donner Memorial State Park (Donner Lake)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites, split among 3 wooded loops
campgrounds.peak_season: Jun – Aug (Lake swimming) & Dec – Mar (Winter snow sports)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Vehicle campground closed Nov–Apr, but park grounds remain fully open for groomed cross-country ski trails, snowshoe rentals, and heated visitor museum. 15 minutes to Palisades Tahoe, Alpine Meadows, Sugar Bowl, and Northstar.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Donner Summit Canyon Trail, Pacific Crest Trail (Donner Pass), Historic China Wall, Emigrant Trail Museum, Truckee River
campgrounds.description: Steeped in pioneer history along the shores of Donner Lake in Truckee. Perfect summer alpine basecamp, and a premier winter snowshoeing destination.

campgrounds.name: Spooner Lake & Sand Harbor Camps
campgrounds.reservation_window: 11 months rolling on ReserveAmerica / Nevada State Parks
campgrounds.site_types: Rustic wilderness cabins & walk-in campsites at Spooner Lake
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Aug & Jan – Feb (Winter XC skiing)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Spooner Lake transforms into a winter wonderland with over 12 km of groomed cross-country ski and snowshoe trails winding through quiet aspen groves and pine forests.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Flume Trail, Marlette Lake, Tahoe Rim Trail, Sand Harbor crystal waters
campgrounds.description: On the scenic East/North Shore of Lake Tahoe. Spooner Lake offers tranquil high-elevation forest camping and winter Nordic trails, with quick access to the Caribbean-blue waters of Sand Harbor.

campgrounds.name: Lassen Volcanic: Manzanita Lake Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov + Loop C/D walk-ins
campgrounds.site_types: Tent, RV (no hookups), 20 rustic camping cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Lassen Park Highway buried under 20+ feet of snow in winter. Snowshoeing and cross-country ski touring from Kohm Yah-mah-nee Visitor Center.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lassen Peak summit (10,457 ft), Bumpass Hell hydrothermal boardwalk, Manzanita Lake loop, Cinder Cone
campgrounds.description: All four volcano types represented! Reflective alpine lake with kayak rentals looking directly at Lassen Peak.

campgrounds.name: Whiskeytown: Oak Bottom Tent Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Walk-in tent sites right on the sandy mountain lakeshore
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter waterfalls flow strongly; crisp lakefront solitude.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Whiskeytown Falls (220-ft cascade), Crystal Creek Falls, kayak tours, Mt. Shasta vistas
campgrounds.description: Crystal-clear mountain lake ringed by pine forests and multi-tier waterfalls; walk-in tent sites right on the sandy shore.

campgrounds.name: Yosemite: Tuolumne Meadows Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: Released on 15th of each month on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Campsites at 8,600 ft along Tuolumne River in High Sierra
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Sep (Only open ~10-12 weeks per year)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Tioga Road (Hwy 120) closes completely Nov–May under 15–20 feet of snow.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lembert Dome, Cathedral Lakes, Lyell Canyon (PCT/JMT), Elizabeth Lake, Tuolumne River
campgrounds.description: The crown jewel of Yosemite's high country at 8,600 feet. Subalpine meadows, glaciated granite domes, and crystalline alpine rivers.

campgrounds.name: Mono Lake & Travertine Hot Springs
campgrounds.reservation_window: Free BLM dispersed camping nearby (Travertine Hot Springs / Bridgeport) & USFS campgrounds at Tioga Pass
campgrounds.site_types: BLM dispersed sites and USFS creek-side campgrounds (Lundy Canyon / Moraine)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Travertine Hot Springs remains accessible in winter. Soaking in natural 103°F mineral pools while surrounded by winter snowdrifts overlooking the Sawtooth Ridge is an iconic Eastern Sierra winter ritual.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: South Tufa Reserve boardwalk, Travertine Hot Springs, Buckeye Hot Springs, Bodie State Historic Park, Lundy Canyon waterfalls
campgrounds.description: Surreal desert-meets-mountain crossroads. Natural hot mineral springs with mountain vistas, eerie tufa towers at Mono Lake, and the remarkably preserved historic ghost town of Bodie.

campgrounds.name: June Lake Loop: Silver Lake Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Campsites nestled under Carson Peak along Silver Lake & Rush Creek
campgrounds.winter_profile: Closed in winter. Prime autumn leaf-peeping location in late September and October.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Rush Creek Trail to Agnew Lake & Gem Lake, Ansel Adams Wilderness, Silver Lake marina
campgrounds.description: Situated at the base of the sheer 10,909-foot Carson Peak along Rush Creek and Silver Lake. Starting point for the Rush Creek Trail into Ansel Adams Wilderness.

campgrounds.name: Lake Shasta: Antlers Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites in oak & pine forest on Sacramento Arm
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; mild winter boating and fishing.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lake Shasta Caverns, Bailey Cove Trail, Shasta Dam, water skiing and houseboating
campgrounds.description: Warm water reservoir recreation surrounded by forested mountain inlets with great swimming and boat access.

campgrounds.name: Trinity Lake: Hayward Flat Camp
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Tent and RV campsites in pine forest along Stuart Fork Arm
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open seasonally May–Oct; serene mountain setting under the Trinity Alps.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Trinity Alps Wilderness trailheads, Trinity River fly fishing, Bowerman Ridge, lake boating
campgrounds.description: Peaceful, uncrowded alternative to Shasta tucked into deep conifer forest under the rugged Trinity Alps.

campgrounds.name: June Lake Loop: Oh! Ridge Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites perched above sandy lake beach
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Aug (Beach) & late Sep – Oct (Golden fall foliage)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Campground closes mid-October due to freezing temperatures. However, June Mountain ski resort opens Dec–April with steep powder bowls.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Parker Lake trail, Fern Lake, Rush Creek Trail into Ansel Adams Wilderness & Thousand Island Lake, Gull Lake
campgrounds.description: Known as the 'Switzerland of California.' Perched on a sandy bluff above June Lake with swimming beach, trout fishing, and views of Carson Peak.

campgrounds.name: Trinity Alps: Bridge Camp Trailhead
campgrounds.reservation_window: FCFS trailhead camping ($10-$15) + Free Wilderness Backpacking Permit
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive trailhead campsites & infinite backcountry wilderness camping
campgrounds.winter_profile: High alpine wilderness frozen under heavy snow in winter; mountaineering only.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Canyon Creek Lakes, Caribou Basin, Stuart Fork Trail to Emerald & Sapphire Lakes
campgrounds.description: The Switzerland of California. Glacial cirques, jagged granite ridges, and azure alpine tarns with uncrowded solitude.

campgrounds.name: Mammoth Lakes: Lake Mary Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Campsites on crystal Lake Mary with marina & paddleboard rentals
campgrounds.winter_profile: Buried in snow in winter; winter cross-country ski trails groomed right across frozen Lake Mary by Tamarack Lodge.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Lake Mary loop, Crystal Crag, Lake George, Panorama Dome
campgrounds.description: Camp right on the shores of Lake Mary, the largest lake in the Mammoth Lakes Basin. Crystal clear waters and alpine peaks.

campgrounds.name: Mammoth Lakes: Coldwater Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites at 9,000 ft elevation along Coldwater Creek
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Aug (Alpine summer) & Nov – Apr (Mammoth ski season)
campgrounds.winter_profile: WORLD-CLASS WINTER SPORTS CAPITAL: Campground closed Oct–May under feet of snow. Mammoth Mountain (11,053 ft) offers 3,500 acres of ski terrain. Winter snowshoeing and XC skiing at Tamarack Lodge.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Duck Pass Trail, Devils Postpile geometric basalt columns, Rainbow Falls (101-ft cascade), Crystal Lake, Mammoth Crest
campgrounds.description: High alpine wonderland at 9,000 feet in the Mammoth Lakes Basin. Direct trailhead access to Duck Pass, Emerald Lake, and Barney Lake.

campgrounds.name: McArthur-Burney Falls State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites, 24 rustic cabins
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; winter snow transforms Burney Falls into an icy fairy tale; heated cabins available.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: 129-foot Burney Falls ('Eighth Wonder of the World'), Lake Britton swim beach, Pacific Crest Trail
campgrounds.description: Roaring 129-foot spring-fed waterfall gushing 100 million gallons of cold water daily from volcanic basalt underground springs.

campgrounds.name: Convict Lake Campground
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Tent and RV sites along Convict Creek beneath towering cliffs
campgrounds.peak_season: Jun – Aug (Summer fishing) & Oct (Fall foliage reflection)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Campground closes in late October. However, the lake road is plowed year-round, allowing breathtaking winter day visits to photograph Mount Morrison's sheer snow-dusted rock face.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Convict Lake Loop Trail, Convict Creek Canyon Trail to Lake Genevieve (John Muir Wilderness), Hot Creek Geologic Site, Whitmore Hot Springs
campgrounds.description: One of the most photogenic alpine lakes in the world. Mount Morrison rises 4,000 vertical feet directly from the shoreline.

campgrounds.name: Castle Crags State Park
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 8:00 AM PT on ReserveCalifornia (some FCFS sites off-season)
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent & RV sites (no hookups)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Open year-round; snow dusts the towering granite crags in winter; lower riverside loop accessible.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Crags Trail to Castle Dome (6,000-ft granite spires), Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), Upper Sacramento River trout fishing
campgrounds.description: Dramatic 6,000-foot granite spires looming above pine forests with jaw-dropping views of snow-capped Mt. Shasta.

campgrounds.name: Big Pine Creek Campground (Palisade Glacier)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent and RV sites along roaring glacier-fed Big Pine Creek (7,700 ft)
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Sep (Glacial lakes thawed into vibrant turquoise)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Campground closed in winter (Nov–Apr); road closed at lower glacier gate due to snow. Extreme mountaineers use it for winter ascents of the Palisade Glacier.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Temple Crag, Big Pine Lakes 1-7, Palisade Glacier, South Fork Big Pine Creek to Brainerd Lake, Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
campgrounds.description: Trailhead for the famed North Fork Big Pine Creek trail to Seven Lakes—fed by Palisade Glacier (the southernmost glacier in North America) giving turquoise-milky waters beneath Temple Crag (12,999 ft).

campgrounds.name: Whitney Portal Campground (Mount Whitney Base)
campgrounds.reservation_window: 6 months rolling at 7:00 AM PT on Recreation.gov (Summit permits via annual lottery in February)
campgrounds.site_types: Drive-in tent sites nestled in thick pine forest at 8,360 ft
campgrounds.peak_season: Jul – Sep (Mount Whitney summit snow-free window)
campgrounds.winter_profile: Whitney Portal Road closes in winter near the base. Heavy snow blankets the canyon; only accessible on foot/skis by experienced technical mountaineers tackling the Mountaineer's Route.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mount Whitney Trail (22 miles round trip, 6,100 ft elevation gain), Lone Pine Lake (no permit required day-hike), Meysan Lake, Alabama Hills
campgrounds.description: The official starting point for hiking Mount Whitney (14,505 ft, highest peak in the contiguous US). Shaded by giant ponderosa and Jeffrey pines alongside roaring waterfalls.

campgrounds.name: Alabama Hills: Movie Flat Dispersed
campgrounds.reservation_window: No reservations - Designated dispersed sites (Free $0). Follow BLM designated camping posts.
campgrounds.site_types: Primitive vehicle dispersed campsites nestled in golden granite boulder mazes
campgrounds.winter_profile: PRIME WINTER CAMPING DESTINATION! While the high Sierra peaks above are frozen under 15 feet of snow, the Alabama Hills enjoy crisp, sunny winter days (55–65°F) and cool nights. Unmatched winter photography with rounded warm rocks framing snow-capped Mount Whitney.
campgrounds.nearby_hikes_attractions: Mobius Arch Loop Trail, Movie Road, Shark's Tooth, Mount Whitney Fish Hatchery, Museum of Western Film History in Lone Pine
campgrounds.description: World-famous golden granite rock arches and rounded labyrinth boulders sitting directly beneath the towering 14,000-foot snow-capped eastern face of the Sierra Nevada.
